items.title: Section: Nine Grounds of Secondary Affliction — Living Together, Correcting Each Other, and Four Wrong Ways to Eat

items.zh: 復次，隨煩惱依處，當知略有九種。一、展轉共住，二、展轉相舉，三、利養，四、邪命，五、不敬尊師，六、不忍，七、毀增上戒，八、毀增上心，九、毀增上慧。
items.en: Furthermore, secondary affliction's grounds should be known as briefly nine: living together in community, mutual correction, others' gain of material support, wrong livelihood, failing to revere one's teachers, lack of compassionate forbearance, violating the higher discipline, violating the higher concentration, and violating the higher wisdom.

items.title: Section: Twenty-Four Secondary Afflictions — Minor, Medium, and Major, All Already Named

items.zh: 復次，隨煩惱自性云何？謂忿、恨、覆、惱、嫉、慳、誑、諂、憍、害、無慚無愧、惛沈、掉舉、不信、懈怠、放逸、忘念、散亂、不正知、惡作、睡眠、尋、伺。如本地分已廣詮說。
items.en: Furthermore, what is secondary affliction's own essential nature? Indignation, grudge-holding, concealment, vexation, envy, stinginess, deceit, flattery, conceit, harmfulness, shamelessness, lack of conscience, dullness, restlessness, lack of faith, laziness, negligence, forgetfulness, distraction, incorrect understanding, remorse, drowsiness, and coarse and subtle discursive thought. As already extensively explained in the Basic Section.

items.zh: 如是等類，名隨煩惱自性。

items.title: Section: Matching Twenty-Four Afflictions to Nine Grounds — Secondary Affliction's Entire Analysis Complete

items.zh: 此中初二，依初依處而生；第三、第四，依第二；第五、第六，依第三；第七、第八，依第四；第九，依第五；第十，依第六；十一、十二，依第七；所餘十二，依後二依處而生。當知此中，毀增上心、毀增上慧由三門轉。一、由毀止相門，二、由毀舉相門，三、由毀捨相門。惛沈、睡眠，由初依處生；掉舉、惡作，由第二依處生；不信乃至尋伺，由第三依處生。復次，隨煩惱云何展轉相應？當知無慚無愧，與一切不善相應。不信、懈怠、放逸、忘念、散亂、惡慧，與一切染污心相應。睡眠、惡作，與一切善、不善、無記相應。所餘當知互不相應。復次，隨煩惱幾世俗有？幾實物有？謂忿、恨、惱、嫉、害是瞋分故，皆世俗有；慳、憍、掉舉是貪分故，皆世俗有；覆、誑、諂、惛沈、睡眠、惡作是癡分故，皆世俗有；無慚無愧、不信、懈怠是實物有；放逸是假有，如前說；忘念、散亂、惡慧是癡分故，一切皆是世俗有；尋伺二種是發語言心加行分故，及慧分故，俱是假有。復次，隨煩惱云何成軟中上品？當知如本煩惱說。如是隨煩惱，若事、若差別、若過失、若所治，隨其所應，皆如煩惱應知。
items.en: The first two arise from the first ground... the remaining twelve arise from the last two grounds. One should know shamelessness and lack of conscience accompany every unwholesome state. Lack of faith, laziness, negligence, forgetfulness, distraction, and corrupted wisdom accompany every defiled state. Drowsiness and remorse accompany wholesome, unwholesome, and neutral states alike. The rest do not co-occur with one another. Indignation, grudge-holding, vexation, envy, and harmfulness are variants of aversion, hence conventional; stinginess, conceit, and restlessness are variants of craving, hence conventional; concealment, deceit, flattery, dullness, drowsiness, and remorse are variants of delusion, hence conventional; shamelessness, lack of conscience, lack of faith, and laziness exist as genuinely distinct realities. As with secondary affliction's grounds, distinctions, harm, and remedy — each, as appropriate, should be understood exactly as with root affliction.

items.title: Section: The Neutral at Last — Four Grounds Where Karma's Ripening, Daily Posture, Livelihood, and Meditation Meet

items.zh: 復次，諸無記法依處，當知略有四種。謂業所引生；生已，若行住、若養命、若三摩地差別。
items.en: Furthermore, neutral phenomena's grounds should be known as briefly four: what is generated by karma; and, once generated, ordinary posture, the sustaining of life, and the distinctions belonging to meditative absorption.

items.title: Section: Four Kinds of Neutral Phenomena, and Why Only Two of Them Ever Occur Together

items.zh: 復次，彼自性云何？謂異熟生蘊，若中庸加行所攝威儀路及工巧處，若為嬉戲加行所攝變化。問：彼云何展轉相應耶？答：威儀路、工巧處，或於一時展轉相應。如說或有事業，行時易作，非住、非坐、亦非偃臥；乃至或有事業，若行、若住、若坐、若臥，皆悉易作。如經廣說。所餘無有展轉相應。問：是諸無記，幾實物有？幾是假有？答：於異熟所攝諸蘊及心加行差別中而施設故，當知一切皆世俗有。
items.en: Furthermore, what is its own essential nature? Karma-ripened aggregates, ordinary posture and livelihood-craft carried out with a neutral disposition, and transformation undertaken for mere amusement. Question: how do these associate with one another? Answer: ordinary posture and livelihood-craft sometimes occur together; the rest do not co-occur with anything. Question: how many of these neutral phenomena are genuinely real, and how many merely provisional? Answer: since all are provisionally designated upon the karma-ripened aggregates or upon distinct activities of mind, one should know all are merely conventional.

items.title: Section: Grading the Neutral, and Twelve Honest Trades From Farming to Music

items.zh: 云何彼成軟中上品？謂異熟生及威儀路不猛利故，俱是軟品；諸工巧處性猛利故，說名中品；當知變化性極猛利，故是上品。又四種類，各有差別。謂無色界異熟是軟品，色界異熟是中品，欲界異熟是上品。若坐、若臥是軟威儀，住是中威儀，行是上威儀。初習業者是下工巧，已串習者是中工巧，堪為師者是上工巧。下品修三摩地所得是軟變化，中品修三摩地所得是中變化，上品修三摩地所得是上變化。如是等類，軟中上品差別應知。問：是諸無記依何事生？答：當知略說依十二事。如聞所成地已說。
items.en:
How do these become soft, medium, and superior grade? Karma-ripened aggregates and ordinary posture, being unforceful, are both soft grade; the various livelihood-crafts, being forceful, are medium grade; and meditative transformation, being extremely forceful, is superior grade. Formless-realm ripening is soft, form-realm ripening is medium, desire-realm ripening is superior. Sitting and lying are soft posture, standing is medium, walking is superior. A beginner is inferior craft, one with sustained practice is medium craft, one capable of teaching is superior craft. Transformation produced by lesser concentration is soft, by medium concentration is medium, by superior concentration is superior.
Question: from how many activities do these neutral phenomena arise? Answer: briefly, from twelve, already explained in the Stage Formed Through Hearing.

blocks.text: Secondary afflictions arise mostly in community life: living together, correcting each other, getting one's needs. Then the "neutral" things: ripening, posture, craft, and supernormal transformation.
Master Cháng Bǎi: when precepts are broken and people accuse one another, concealment and vexation easily arise; and obtaining one's needs by improper means is wrong livelihood.
Master Cháng Bǎi: without compassion, unable to bear another's actions, one gives rise to harm and vexation.
The treatise lists them without classifying; Master Cháng Bǎi groups them as minor, major, and indeterminate (remorse, drowsiness, discursive thought).
Shamelessness and lack of conscience accompany every unwholesome state; drowsiness and remorse accompany all three moral qualities.

What karma generates; posture; sustaining life; and the distinctions of absorption. Master Cháng Bǎi spells these out: the ripened aggregates, the four postures, the crafts, and supernormal transformations.
Master Cháng Bǎi: posture and craft are marked by a neutral disposition; transformation done for amusement is neutral.

By forcefulness. Master Cháng Bǎi: ripening and posture act naturally, without force, and are "soft"; supernormal transformation needs strong absorption and is "superior". Desire-realm results are coarse in body and mind, and so "superior" in this sense.
Most secondary afflictions in the list arise from living with others. Community is where practice is tested.

quiz.q: What are the nine grounds of secondary affliction?
options: living together, mutual correction, material gain, wrong livelihood, irreverence, lack of forbearance, violating higher discipline, mind, and wisdom
the nine attainments, the four absorptions, four formless, and cessation, secondary afflictions differing with the height of absorption
the nine fetters: craving through stinginess
the nine abodes of beings
quiz.why: The treatise lists nine grounds, mostly settings of community life. Master Cháng Bǎi: when precepts are broken and people accuse one another, concealment and vexation easily arise; and obtaining one's needs by improper means is wrong livelihood. The list shows secondary afflictions arising in ordinary relations among practitioners.

quiz.q: The English has "lack of compassionate forbearance" for 不忍 and "attachment to material support" for 利養. How do these compare with the lecture?
options: both are exact: 利養 is one's own attachment to offerings, the lecture calling it a form of craving, with no idea of envy
"compassionate" is an apt addition to 不忍; 利養 is being unable to bear others' gain, so "attachment" is off
不忍 should be "impatience with pain"; 利養 should be "farming"
both are additions, absent from the treatise
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: with no compassion towards beings and unable to bear another's bodily and verbal acts, one gives rise to harm and vexation; so "compassionate" is a useful addition. But on 利養 he says: unable to bear another's gain, one gives rise to envy. The English "attachment" points to craving for one's own gain, which leaves out what this ground produces.

quiz.q: The treatise lists twenty-four secondary afflictions in one run. How does Master Cháng Bǎi group them?
options: minor: dullness through incorrect understanding; major: indignation through harm; indeterminate: remorse, drowsiness, and discursive thought
minor: indignation through harm; major: dullness through incorrect understanding; indeterminate: remorse, drowsiness, and discursive thought
all are major, joined with every defiled mind, with no minor or indeterminate class at all
three groups by the three poisons
quiz.why: The treatise lists the twenty-four without classifying them; the grouping is the lecturer's. He names ten minor secondary afflictions, eight major, and the indeterminate factors remorse, drowsiness, and discursive thought. Shamelessness and lack of conscience fall between. The English overview attributes this grouping to "the treatise," which is not accurate.

quiz.q: With what states are shamelessness and lack of conscience, and drowsiness and remorse, associated?
options: shamelessness and lack of conscience with all three; drowsiness and remorse with the unwholesome only, drowsiness always being evil
shamelessness and lack of conscience with every unwholesome state; drowsiness and remorse with wholesome, unwholesome, and neutral alike
all four with the neutral alone
all four join neither one another nor anything else
quiz.why: The treatise says shamelessness and lack of conscience accompany every unwholesome state, and drowsiness and remorse accompany all three moral qualities. Master Cháng Bǎi: when desire-realm beings create evil karma through the sixth consciousness, shamelessness and lack of conscience are surely present. The rest differ in nature and arise separately, and so are said not to be associated.

quiz.q: Which secondary afflictions are real, and to what do the rest belong?
options: shamelessness, lack of conscience, lack of faith, laziness are real; indignation and the like are variants of aversion, stinginess of craving, concealment of delusion, all conventional
indignation, grudge, vexation, envy, harm are real; shamelessness and the rest are conventional, being mere absences of good
all twenty-four are real
all twenty-four are conventional
quiz.why: The treatise assigns variants of aversion, craving, and delusion as conventional, and names shamelessness, lack of conscience, lack of faith, and laziness as real. Note the lecturer's remark that 不正知 in the list and 惡慧 here are equivalent; the English "incorrect understanding" for both hides that the Chinese changes words.

quiz.q: What are the four grounds of neutral phenomena?
options: giving, discipline, patience, and diligence, since these need neither affliction nor a good mind, and so are neutral
the four elements
what karma generates; and once generated, posture, sustaining life, and the distinctions of absorption
the three realms and the uncontaminated
quiz.why: The treatise names what karma generates, and then posture, sustaining life, and the distinctions of absorption. Master Cháng Bǎi spells these out: the ripened five aggregates; the four postures; the crafts of scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants by which life is sustained; and transformations produced through absorption by a neutral mind.

quiz.q: By what wording does the treatise mark neutral posture, craft, and transformation, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: posture and craft by "amusement"; transformation by "neutral disposition," since transformation most needs a middle mind
posture and craft by "neutral disposition," excluding good and evil; transformation by "amusement," excluding good
all by "benefiting others"
all by "generated by karma"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: posture and craft are marked by a neutral disposition, which excludes the good and evil kinds; transformation is marked by amusement, which excludes the good kind, as transformation done with a neutral mind for play. So the same activities could be wholesome or defiled with another intention, as §44 says.

quiz.q: How do neutral phenomena become soft, medium, and superior?
options: transformation, unforceful, is soft; crafts medium; ripening and posture, extremely forceful, superior, results being heaviest
by length of life: short soft, medium medium, long superior
by moral quality: unwholesome soft, neutral medium, wholesome superior
ripening and posture, unforceful, are soft; crafts, forceful, medium; transformation, extremely forceful, superior
quiz.why: The treatise grades by forcefulness. Master Cháng Bǎi: the ripened aggregates and postures act naturally, without force, and so are soft; supernormal transformation needs strong absorption and a very forceful mind, and so is superior. The grades measure intensity of activity, not value.

quiz.q: The English has "desire-realm ripening is superior." How might "superior" mislead?
options: it may suggest the desire realm is better; the lecture says it is superior through coarseness of body and mind, the grade being intensity, not worth
it does not mislead: the desire realm truly surpasses the others, buddhas appearing only there, so the English is exact
it should be "inferior," the treatise really saying the desire realm is low
上品 means the longest lifespan
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the results of the desire realm are coarse in body and mind, and so are of superior grade. Thus the ordering runs against what "superior" suggests in English: formless ripening, which is highest as a realm, is soft. Here the grade measures coarseness and force. "Strong" or "intense" would avoid the confusion.
